back: Price = cost per unit + a percentage mark-up on cost.
Charging a price similar to, or slightly below, competitors' prices.
A low price at launch to win market share quickly, raised later.
A high price at launch for a new, unique product, lowered later as rivals arrive.
Prices that change frequently with demand at the time, often online (fares, hotel rooms).
Total cost ÷ output, where total cost = fixed costs + variable costs.
Mark-up = gross profit ÷ cost × 100. Margin = gross profit ÷ selling price × 100.
Consider how new and unique the product is, competitors, costs, customers' incomes and whether demand varies by time.
Ignores competitors' prices and what customers will pay; if fewer units sell, average cost rises.
